text: This lesson gives FeedbackScope a real Dockerfile, builds it, pushes it, and deploys it -- the first full pass through everything Chapters 1 through 3 covered, on one actual project.

Stage one, the builder, installs every Python package, including any compilers pip needs along the way. None of those build tools make it into the final image -- only the installed packages get copied forward.

Stage two is the runtime image. That RUN line downloads and caches the model weights at build time, not on first request -- trading a bigger image for a running container that never pays a model-download delay later.
Build, tag with a real version -- v1, not latest -- and push to the registry. A specific tag is what gives Lesson 16's rollback something concrete to roll back to.
Deploying is Lesson 12's two-screen pattern again: point the platform at the pushed image and its port, and wire in a real health check endpoint for the platform to poll.
This deploy is deliberately minimal -- one instance, defaults only, no caching. That's exactly what's missing, and exactly what Lesson 24 adds next: a real autoscaling policy.
